answer.generated: An entity relationship diagram (ERD) serves as a visual representation of the conceptual and logical design of a database, illustrating the relationships between entities and their attributes. ERDs are crucial during the logical design phase as they facilitate the transformation of the conceptual design into a structured, normalized schema. By depicting entities, their attributes, and relationships, ERDs enable designers to identify and eliminate redundancy, ensuring a robust and efficient database structure. For instance, an ERD might show how the entity "University" relates to "Student" through the relationship "Enrollment," which helps in designing a well-normalized schema. The ERD thus acts as a bridge between the high-level conceptual design and the detailed logical design, guiding the process of converting abstract data models into a practical, implementable database schema.
